Subject: Depression over coastal Myanmar and adjoining Northeast Bay of Bengal & 
southeast Bangladesh  weakened in to a Well  Marked Low Pressure Area over  North 
Myanmar and adjoining areas of south east Bangladesh , Mizoram & Northeast Bay of 
Bengal 
The Depression over coastal Myanmar and adjoining Northeast Bay of Bengal & southeast 
Bangladesh moved north-northwestwards and weakened into a Well Marked Low Pressure Area 
over North Myanmar and adjoining areas of southeast Bangladesh, Mizoram & Northeast Bay of 
Bengal at 0530 hrs IST of today, the 30th September 2026. 
It is very likely to move north -northwestwards towards Mizoram, Tripura & adjoining southeast 
Bangladesh and weaken gradually into a Low Pressure Area during next 24 hours.  
Warnings: 
 
(i) Rainfall Warning: 
❖ Light to moderate rainfall at many places with isolated heavy rainfall very likely over Assam & 
Meghalaya, Nagaland, Mizoram & Tripura on 30th September. 
 
(ii) Wind warning: 
❖ Squally weather with wind speed reaching 25-35 kmph gusting to 45 kmph over northeast Bay 
of Bengal and along & off Myanmar-Bangladesh coast on 30th September, 2026 and decrease 
gradually thereafter. 
(iii) Sea condition: 
 
❖ Rough to moderate sea condition is very likely over adjoining areas of Northeast Bay of Bengal 
and along & off Myanmar – Bangladesh coasts during next 6 hours and improve thereafter. 
 
India Meteorological Department 
 (Ministry of Earth Sciences) 
 

(iv) Fishermen warnings: 
Fishermen are advised not to venture into northeast Bay of Bengal and along & off Myanmar- 
Bangladesh coasts on 30th September, 2026.  
(v) Impact expected & Action Suggested (Assam & Meghalaya, Nagaland, Mizoram and 
Tripura for squally winds & heavy rainfall): 
Impact expected: 
❖ Breaking of tree branches, uprooting of small trees like banana, papaya, drum sticks. 
❖ Strong wind and rain may damage plantation, horticulture and standing crops. 
❖ Partial damage to vulnerable structures due to strong winds and rain. 
❖ There could be localised landslides, mudslides, landslips in hilly areas and water logging, 
inundation and flooding over low-lying areas. 
❖ Small ships, trawlers and boats may be affected. 
❖ Occasional reduction in visibility due to heavy rainfall. 
❖ Helicopter services may get affected. 
 
Action suggested: 
❖ People are advised to keep a watch on the weather for worsening conditions and be ready to 
move to safer places accordingly.  
❖ Surface transport may be regulated. 
❖ Fishing operation may be suspended on 30th September.  
❖ Tourism and recreational activities to be regulated. 
❖ Helicopter services to be regulated. 
 
This is the last update about the system. However, regular bulletins/messages regarding 
the remnant Well Marked Low Pressure Area will continue from National Weather 
Forecasting Centre/Regional Meteorological Centres/Meteorological Centres. 
  
 
(Shashi Kant) 
IMD, New Delhi
